claims.text: The initial microstructure consists of dual-phase lamellar colonies.
Controlled solidification using optimized cooling rates and thermal gradients will optimize the lamellar-colony architecture.
Optimized lamellar-colony architecture will reduce microcracking during room-temperature tensile deformation.
Optimized lamellar-colony architecture will enhance cohesion of internal boundaries.
Reduced microcracking and enhanced internal-boundary cohesion will improve strength.
Reduced microcracking and enhanced internal-boundary cohesion will improve room-temperature tensile ductility.
The intervention will increase strength by 20% relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
The intervention will increase tensile ductility by 30% relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
The proposed intervention is applicable at cooling rates between 10 and 100 K/s.
The proposed intervention is applicable at thermal gradients between 1 and 10 K/mm.
The relationship between cooling rate, thermal gradient, and resulting microstructure is not well established.
Microstructural features other than lamellar-colony architecture may influence the mechanical properties.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts 20% higher strength and 30% higher ductility, but the falsification rule only rejects increases below 10% and 20%, respectively. Thus, outcomes that materially miss the stated predictions could still be treated as non-falsifying.
